_comment: Three briefs; two are deliberately flawed, so the linter exits 1.

briefs.summary: A webhook delivery that receives a 503 is retried twice instead of once
briefs.current_behavior: When the receiving endpoint answers 503, the dispatcher schedules a retry from the failure callback and again from the timeout watchdog, so the receiver gets two identical retries about 30 seconds apart.
briefs.desired_behavior: Each failed delivery attempt schedules exactly one retry, regardless of which failure path observes the error. Retries keep the existing backoff schedule and carry the same idempotency key as the original attempt.
key_interfaces: `DeliveryAttempt` status transitions: an attempt may move to `retry_scheduled` at most once
acceptance_criteria: A 503 response produces exactly one scheduled retry for that attempt
A timeout followed by a late 503 for the same attempt produces exactly one scheduled retry
Every retry carries the idempotency key of the original delivery
The existing backoff delays (10s, 30s, 90s) are unchanged
out_of_scope: Changing the retry schedule or maximum attempt count
Dead-letter queue behaviour after the final attempt

briefs.desired_behavior: Open the file src/export/csv_writer.py and go to line 88, then add a buffer.
acceptance_criteria: Export works correctly and is faster

briefs.summary: Rate-limit headers are missing from 429 responses on the public API
briefs.current_behavior: 429 responses from the public API carry no `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header, so clients cannot back off.
briefs.desired_behavior: Every 429 response from the public API includes `Retry-After` in seconds and `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`.
acceptance_criteria: A request over the limit receives a 429 with a `Retry-After` header
The `Retry-After` value equals the seconds until the window resets
